content.title: What is Python?
content.body: Python is a programming language — a way of writing instructions that computers can understand. It was created in 1991 and named after Monty Python, a comedy group (not the snake!). Today it's one of the most popular programming languages in the world.

content.title: Python reads like English
content.body: One reason beginners love Python is that it looks almost like plain English. You don't need lots of special symbols or strange punctuation to get started. The instructions you write are close to the instructions you'd give a person — just a little more precise.

content.title: Python is everywhere
content.body: YouTube, Instagram, Spotify, and NASA all use Python. Scientists use it to analyse data. Game developers use it to build tools. AI systems are often built with it. Learning Python opens a lot of doors — and it's a genuinely great first language.

content.title: Your first look at Python
content.body:
print("Welcome to Python!")

name = "Alex"
print(name + " found a treasure chest!")

content.title: You're ready to start!
content.body: Everything you've just read — what programs are, how computers follow instructions, and what Python looks like — is the foundation. In the next lessons you'll start writing real Python code. Let's go!
